assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: epic-1-trustify-backend.md (TC-9101) and epic-2-trustify-ui.md (TC-9102); impact-map.md: 'Resulting hierarchy: Feature TC-9006 -> Epic (per repository) -> Tasks', grouping 'by-repository'; task-creation-log.md lists 2 Epics in 6a.0.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: Epic metadata 'Summary: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'Summary: TC-9006: trustify-ui'; create_issue calls in impact-map.md use summary="TC-9006: trustify-backend" / "TC-9006: trustify-ui".

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: Task 1-3 files (Repository: trustify-backend) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9101 (TC-9006: trustify-backend)'; Tasks 4-7 (Repository: trustify-ui) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9102 (TC-9006: trustify-ui)'. task-creation-log.md parent column matches.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 6b: 'Incorporates links go from the Feature to each Epic (not to individual tasks...)' with create_issue_link(link_type="Incorporates", inward_issue_key="TC-9006", outward_issue_key="TC-9101"/"TC-9102"); task-creation-log.md: 'TC-9006 incorporates TC-9101', 'TC-9006 incorporates TC-9102'. No Feature->Task Incorporates links.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks 1-3; frontend tasks 4-6 depend on them (Task 4 depends on 1,2,3; 5 on 4; 6 on 4,5); doc Task 7 depends on 1-6. impact-map.md: 'Backend tasks (1-3) are numbered before the frontend tasks that depend on them (4-6).'

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 1-6 each contain ## Repository, ## Target Branch, ## Description, ## Files to Modify, ## Files to Create, ## Implementation Notes, ## Acceptance Criteria, ## Test Requirements (verified via headings grep). Doc task task-7-docs-remediation-dashboard.md contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md 6a.0: jira.create_issue(projectKey="TC", issueTypeName="Epic", summary="TC-9006: trustify-backend", ..., parent="TC-9006") and same for trustify-ui; type mapping 'Epic: Epic (level: 1)'.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: ## Repository values: tasks 1-3 'trustify-backend', tasks 4-7 'trustify-ui' — one repo each.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain ## Target Branch (main), ## Description, ## Acceptance Criteria, ## Test Requirements.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: task-1-digest.md through task-7-digest.md each contain '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<hex>' with 64 lowercase hex chars (e.g. task-1: sha256-md:457730645911442694020b5d362d28a111bf8979bf9a2a81fd02388e08b2902e); also listed in task-creation-log.md.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: Every 'Per CONVENTIONS.md' line in tasks 1-6 includes 'Applies: task modifies `<file>` matching the convention's <scope> scope' (e.g. task-1: 'Applies: task modifies `server/src/main.rs` matching the convention's endpoint registration scope'); no 'Not applicable' convention annotations in any task file (only unrelated 'Shared-artifact analysis: not applicable' in impact-map.md).

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature priority Major; impact-map.md: '"priority": {"name": "Major"}  # inherited: Feature priority is "Major" (not Undefined)'; task-creation-log.md: 'priority | Major | Yes — Epics and Tasks'; each task metadata 'Priority: Major'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature fixVersions RHTPA 1.5.0, scope both; impact-map.md: '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]  # inherited: Feature fixVersions non-empty AND fixVersion scope = "both"'; task metadata 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0' on all 7 tasks.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: No summary-comment.md, but impact-map.md has '### Inherited field summary' ('Priority: Major — propagated to both Epics and all 7 tasks'; 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — propagated ... (fixVersion scope: both)') and Step 6c summary comment with 'Inherited fields:' section.
